name: Spectrolite
physical: Kept nearby for a sense of calm
summary: Spectrolite is Finland's full-spectrum labradorite, a black stone flashing every color of the rainbow, loved for vision, intuition and creative spark.
intro: Spectrolite is labradorite taken to its most brilliant extreme. The stone has a very dark, almost black body, and when it is turned the whole spectrum blazes out: electric blue, gold, orange, red, green, and violet. The effect is the same labradorescence seen in other labradorite, but spectrolite shows a far wider, richer range of colors. It is found mostly in the Ylämaa area of Finland and in a few places in Russia, and the best slabs are polished into cabochons and sculptures. It is firmer than most feldspars and takes a wonderful polish. For many collectors, spectrolite is the apex of the labradorite family.
history: Spectrolite got its name in the 1940s, when Finnish geologists and gem dealers began to separate the vividly colored labradorite found near Ylämaa from the more muted material of Canada. The stone had been known locally for a long time, but a railway cut in the area exposed a rich deposit, and the name stuck as a trade term for the multicolor variety. Finnish designers used it in jewelry and in decorative interiors, and the Finnish Gem Society later promoted it as a national gemstone. Many of the older Northern Lights legends told of Canadian labradorite are retold about Finnish spectrolite too, because both flash colors like the aurora.
meaning: Practitioners treat spectrolite as the more intense cousin of labradorite. Its full-spectrum flash is said to bring the clarity of many colors together, helping you see a problem from every side. It is traditionally linked to the Third Eye, Crown, and Throat chakras and used for intuition, visionary work, and creative breakthroughs. People turn to it during times of big change, saying it helps them hold steady while they sort out what comes next. It is also used as a shield, believed to deflect the emotional static of crowded places. Because the stone is dark and deep, it is often chosen for shadow-work and night meditation. Its energy is described as bright, courageous, and slightly electric.
howToUse: Hold spectrolite under a lamp during meditation and let your eyes follow the flash. Wear it as a pendant to bring a sense of protective focus into crowded spaces. Place a slab on your desk as inspiration for creative work, or set one on an altar with a candle to see its colors flare. In a crystal grid, use spectrolite as a center stone with amethyst and clear quartz for an intuition layout. Some people keep a small piece beside the bed for dreamwork. A palm stone is excellent for journaling sessions.
care: Spectrolite is Mohs 6 to 6.5 and shares the cleavage of other feldspars, so avoid knocks and store it separately. A short lukewarm rinse is fine; dry it quickly and avoid ultrasonic cleaners. Cleanse with moonlight, sound, or smoke. Sunlight does not harm it, but heat and sudden temperature changes can stress internal fractures. Polish with a soft cloth only, and keep it away from harsh chemicals or abrasive cleaners that may dull its mirror finish.
identify: Real spectrolite has a very dark body with a flash covering most of the spectrum, often including reds and oranges that ordinary labradorite rarely shows. Ordinary labradorite typically flashes blue and green on a lighter grey base. Glass imitations flash uniformly in every direction. Some dealers label any bright labradorite as spectrolite, so ask for the origin: true spectrolite is traditionally from Finland. A strong flash visible from multiple angles on a nearly black base is a good sign.

faq.q: What is the difference between spectrolite and labradorite?
faq.a: Spectrolite is a high-grade labradorite from Finland with a nearly black body and a full-spectrum flash. Ordinary labradorite is lighter grey and usually shows only blue and green. They are chemically the same mineral.

Spectrolite is traditionally used for intuition, visionary work, and creative inspiration. People also keep it as a protective stone for crowded places and as a companion during times of big personal change.

faq.q: How do I care for spectrolite?
faq.a: Rinse briefly in lukewarm water and dry it at once. Avoid ultrasonic cleaners, knocks, and long soaks because of its cleavage. Cleanse with moonlight, sound, or smoke, and store it apart from harder stones to prevent scratches.
